answer: Divergent-Behavior Ledger. Each identity must publish a signed history of its actions; the protocol periodically challenges random pairs to prove they followed identical rules. Clones cannot diverge, so colluding copies produce identical outputs, exposing shared control. Honest agents reach a unique zenith of unique behavior over time. To fake diversity, an attacker must run each clone through a distinct karst of environmental inputs and decision paths, costing full compute per identity. A yarrow-thin budget cannot sustain this,
